question: What is metformin most commonly prescribed for worldwide?
answers: Treating type II diabetes (as a glucose-lowering agent)

receipt.quote: Metformin is the most commonly prescribed glucose-lowering agent worldwide for the treatment of type II diabetes.

question: Metformin is associated with activation of which kinase, although it is unclear if this is its primary target?

receipt.quote: Notably, metformin is associated with activation of adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), although it is unclear if this is the primary target (Zhou et al., 2001; Ferrannini, 2014; Foretz et al., 2019).

question: In the widely discussed 2013 mouse study of metformin, what changes did metformin produce that might explain its effect on lifespan? Name one.
answers: Transcriptomic changes similar to caloric restriction

receipt.quote: Metformin produced transcriptomic changes similar to those induced by caloric restriction, increased antioxidant defences, preserved mitochondrial function, and inhibited chronic inflammation, all of which may have been involved in the mechanisms underlying its reported effects on lifespan (Martin-Montalvo et al., 2013).

question: In the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study of people with prediabetes, was metformin associated with differences in all-cause mortality after 19–21 years?
answers: No, metformin was not associated with any difference in all-cause, cardiovascular or cancer mortality

receipt.quote: After 19–21 years of follow-up, 453 deaths had occurred in DPPOS participants, and metformin treatment was not associated with any differences in cardiovascular (HR = 1.08), cancer (HR = 1.04) or all-cause mortality (HR = 0.99) (Lee et al., 2021).
